description: What an IDE provides, the role of compilers, interpreters and assemblers, and types of programming error.
content_html:
The Integrated Development Environment

Professional programmers do not write code in a plain text editor. They use an integrated development environment (IDE). An IDE brings together all the tools needed to write, run, test and debug a program in a single interface. Understanding what an IDE provides — and why each tool matters — is a key topic in your exam.

Tools in an IDE

IDEs typically include the following tools. You need to know what each one does:

ToolWhat it does
Code editorWhere code is typed; usually provides syntax highlighting and auto-completion to reduce errors
Syntax error detectionHighlights invalid syntax in real time (e.g. a missing colon in Python) before the program is run
DebuggerSteps through the program one line at a time so the programmer can see exactly what each instruction does
BreakpointA marker placed on a line of code; the debugger pauses execution at that point so the programmer can inspect variable values
Variable watchDisplays the current value of selected variables as the program runs step by step — essential for spotting logic errors
Memory inspectorShows what is stored in memory at runtime; useful for finding memory leaks or unexpected values in low-level work
Key Fact

A breakpoint pauses program execution at a specific line; the variable watch then shows the current value of each variable at that point. Together these are the most powerful IDE debugging tools — they allow a programmer to inspect the program’s internal state at any moment.

Translators: Compiler, Interpreter and Assembler

Every high-level or assembly language program must be translated into machine code before the processor can run it. There are three types of translator, each with a different method:

A compiler reads the entire source code, checks it for errors, and produces a standalone machine code file (an executable). Once compiled, the program can run without the compiler — and typically runs faster because translation is already done. Compilation errors are reported all at once after the whole program has been analysed.

An interpreter reads and executes the program one line at a time. Each line is translated then immediately run. If an error is found, execution stops at that line — which makes interpreters useful for debugging, because the programmer sees exactly which line caused the problem. However, interpreted programs run more slowly because translation happens every time.

An assembler converts assembly language into machine code. Unlike a compiler or interpreter, an assembler works with low-level mnemonics rather than human-readable statements. One assembly instruction translates to one (or a small number of) machine code instructions.

FeatureCompilerInterpreter
TranslatesWhole program at onceOne line at a time
OutputA standalone executable fileNo output file — runs directly
Error reportingAll errors after full translationStops at the first error found
Execution speedFaster (already machine code)Slower (translating at runtime)
Source code needed at runtime?NoYes
Typical useC, C++ — final software releasePython — development and scripting

Python uses an interpreter by default, which is why running a Python program always requires Python to be installed on the machine.

Compilation Stages

A compiler does not translate code in one magic step. It passes the source code through several distinct stages, each preparing it for the next:

StageWhat happens
Lexical analysisSource code is broken into tokens (keywords, identifiers, operators). Comments and whitespace are removed.
Syntax analysisTokens are checked against the grammar rules of the language; a parse tree is built. Syntax errors are reported here.
Semantic analysisThe parse tree is checked for meaning: are variables declared before use? Do data types match? Semantic errors are caught here.
Code generationThe parse tree is translated into intermediate or machine code.
Code optimisationThe generated code is improved to run faster or use less memory, without changing what it does.
Key Fact

The five compilation stages in order are: lexical analysis (tokenise), syntax analysis (grammar check), semantic analysis (meaning check), code generation (translate), and code optimisation (improve). Each stage must succeed for the next to begin.

Types of Programming Error

Errors in programs are classified by when and how they occur. Your exam includes several specific error types — know the definition and an example for each.

Syntactical (syntax) error: The code breaks the grammar rules of the language. The translator cannot even parse the code. Example: missing a colon at the end of a Python if statement.

Logical error: The code runs without crashing but produces the wrong result. The programmer’s reasoning is flawed. Example: writing SET total = total - item when addition was intended. Logic errors are the hardest to find because the program appears to work.

Runtime error: The code is syntactically and logically correct but something goes wrong during execution, causing the program to crash. Example: dividing by zero, or trying to open a file that does not exist.

Linking error: The program references an external library or module that cannot be found or does not match. Example: calling a function from a library that has not been installed or imported correctly.

Rounding error: A calculation loses precision because floating-point numbers cannot represent all decimal values exactly in binary. Example: in Python, 0.1 + 0.2 does not equal exactly 0.3 due to binary floating-point representation.

Truncation error: A number is shortened (truncated) rather than rounded, losing information beyond a certain point. Example: storing the result 7.9 as an integer gives 7, not 8 — the fractional part is discarded, not rounded.
exam_tip_html: In questions about translators, make an explicit contrast between compilers and interpreters — “unlike a compiler, which translates the whole program before it runs, an interpreter translates and executes one line at a time.” For compilation stages, give them in order: lexical → syntax → semantic → code generation → optimisation. For error types, the distinction between a runtime error (crashes during execution) and a logical error (wrong output, no crash) is a very common exam question — prepare a concrete example of each.
conclusion_html:
Key Takeaways

  • An IDE provides a code editor, syntax error detection, debugger, breakpoints, variable watch and memory inspector — all in one application to speed up development and testing.
  • A compiler translates the whole program at once; an interpreter works line by line. An assembler converts assembly language to machine code. The five compilation stages are: lexical analysis, syntax analysis, semantic analysis, code generation, optimisation.
  • Programming errors include syntactical (grammar), logical (wrong result), runtime (crash during execution), linking (missing library), rounding (floating-point imprecision) and truncation (fractional part discarded).

practice_questions.text:
Which IDE tool pauses program execution at a specific line so the programmer can inspect variable values?
A) Syntax error detection
B) Memory inspector
C) Breakpoint
D) Code editor
State the difference between a compiler and an interpreter.
practice_questions.marks:
Compiler: translates the entire program at once / produces a standalone executable [1].
Interpreter: translates and executes the program one line at a time / requires source code at runtime [1].

practice_questions.text:
A student writes the following Python code:

x = 10
y = 0
print(x / y)

Identify the type of error this will produce and explain why.
practice_questions.marks:
Runtime error [1] because the code is syntactically correct and will pass translation [1], but dividing by zero causes the program to crash during execution [1]. A syntax or logic error would not apply here since the grammar is valid and the logic of dividing x by y is what was intended [1].
Mastering: Correct error type, explained with both why it is not syntax and why it occurs at runtime.
Secure: Correct error type with one valid reason.
Developing: Correct error type without explanation.
Emerging: Partially correct.

practice_questions.text: Describe what happens during the lexical analysis and syntax analysis stages of compilation.
practice_questions.marks:
Lexical analysis: source code is broken into tokens (keywords, identifiers, operators) [1]; comments and whitespace are removed [1].
Syntax analysis: tokens are checked against the grammar rules of the language [1]; a parse tree is built / syntax errors are identified and reported [1].
Award up to 3 marks from the four marking points above.

practice_questions.text: Explain two advantages of using an IDE compared to a plain text editor when writing a program.
practice_questions.marks:
Up to 2 marks per advantage:
- Syntax error detection highlights mistakes in real time / before running, saving time finding typos [1 + 1].
- Debugger and breakpoints allow step-by-step execution / makes finding logical and runtime errors much faster than reading code manually [1 + 1].
- Variable watch shows values at each step / removes need to add temporary print statements to inspect variables [1 + 1].
Mastering: Two distinct advantages, each developed.
Secure: Two advantages, one developed.
Developing: One developed advantage.
Emerging: One simple relevant point.

practice_questions.text: Compare how a compiler and an interpreter handle errors. Discuss which approach is more useful when a programmer is still developing and testing their code.
practice_questions.marks:
Mastering: Explicit contrast of error handling (compiler reports all errors after full translation; interpreter stops at the first error, identifying the exact line); argues interpreter is more useful during development (immediate feedback, easier to locate the specific error line, no recompile step); acknowledges compiler advantage for final release (faster execution, no source code needed); justified conclusion — 5-6 marks.
Secure: One contrast and one argument for interpreter advantage, some development — 3-4 marks.
Developing: Correct description of one translator's error handling — 2 marks.
Emerging: A relevant point about one translator — 1 mark.

knowledge_checks.q: Which compilation stage checks that tokens follow the grammar rules of the programming language?
A program runs but gives the wrong answer. No error message appears. What type of error is this?
An interpreter translates and executes a program _____ at a time, stopping if an error is encountered.
A _____ error occurs when a program crashes during execution, such as when it tries to divide by zero.
Match each term to its correct description:
right: Fractional part of a number is discarded, losing information
A marker that pauses execution so variables can be inspected
First compilation stage: source code broken into tokens

flashcard_questions.a: Software combining a code editor, debugger and other tools into one application for writing and testing programs.

flashcard_questions.q: What does a breakpoint do in an IDE?
flashcard_questions.a: Pauses program execution at a specific line so the programmer can inspect variable values.

flashcard_questions.q: What does the variable watch tool show in an IDE?
flashcard_questions.a: The current value of selected variables as the program runs step by step.

flashcard_questions.q: How does a compiler differ from an interpreter in the way it translates code?
flashcard_questions.a: A compiler translates the whole program at once; an interpreter translates and runs it one line at a time.

flashcard_questions.q: Does a compiled program need the compiler to run again after compilation?
flashcard_questions.a: No — it produces a standalone executable that runs without the compiler.
It translates assembly language mnemonics into machine code.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the first stage of compilation?
flashcard_questions.a: Lexical analysis — source code is broken into tokens and whitespace/comments are removed.

flashcard_questions.q: Which compilation stage catches errors such as using a variable before it is declared?
flashcard_questions.a: Semantic analysis — it checks the meaning and consistency of the code.
An error where code breaks the grammar rules of the language, preventing translation.
An error where the program runs without crashing but produces the wrong result.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the difference between a rounding error and a truncation error?
flashcard_questions.a: Rounding loses precision due to floating-point limits; truncation discards the fractional part entirely.
An error that causes a program to crash during execution, such as dividing by zero.

glossary_terms.definition: Software that combines a code editor, debugger, error checker and other tools into one application to help programmers write, test and fix programs.
A translator that converts an entire high-level program into machine code in one step before the program runs; the resulting executable does not need the compiler to run again.
A translator that converts and executes a high-level program one line at a time; the source code must be present every time the program runs.
A translator that converts assembly language mnemonics into machine code, one instruction at a time.
